units.title: Co-op calls in outside crews after worst night of cuts
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op has brought in line crews from outside the Sound after the worst night of power cuts this month, in which four separate circuits failed and some homes in Gilliver and on Lisle were without electricity for more than four hours.

units.author: courier
units.text: About 2,200 customers lost supply at some point between 22:48 and 03:16. The Port Ammet north feeder, which serves the streets behind the market and part of the hospital site, was off for more than two hours. The inland Brackwater feeder, which also supplies the reservoir pumping station, failed shortly after midnight.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op said four crews from a neighbouring network would arrive today and stay 'for as long as necessary'. Asked why an inland circuit had failed if the cause was coastal salt, a spokesperson repeated that 'other contributing factors are being examined' and said a full technical report would follow.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, the village hall opened overnight for two elderly residents who rely on powered equipment. 'We had tea, a radio and the hall generator, and we had a very nice time,' said one volunteer. 'But nobody should have to leave their house at one in the morning because the lights went.'

units.author: courier
units.text: The change in the weather today, with rain and stronger winds forecast for several days, is expected to bring the salt and damp the co-op has blamed throughout. Linemen have privately told the Courier that this will make it harder, not easier, to say what has been causing the faults.

units.title: Live: rain, wind and another night of cuts
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:20. Rain has set in across the Sound and the wind is picking up from the south. The reservoir lane at Brackwater is closed by flooding at the culvert works; use the Tollinby road. So far the power is holding. We'll be here all night either way.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 23:55. A brief cut on the Gilliver spur just before midnight, back within about a minute. Listeners on the front say the street lamps dimmed to orange for the best part of a minute before it went, and the night ferry, coming in at the time, kept its own deck lights burning throughout.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 01:35. Gilliver and the Holm road are off again, and this time it hasn't come back by itself. The co-op says a crew is on the way to the switch. Carrow Point and the coast road are also reporting a cut. Rain heavy here in Port Ammet.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 02:10. Power back for Gilliver after thirty-eight minutes. Carrow Point is still off. A listener there says she's sitting by the window watching the lighthouse beam go round 'as if nothing's happened', which, for an automated light with its own batteries, it hasn't.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 03:08. One more short cut on the Gilliver spur, about a minute, then back. Carrow Point and the coast road were restored just before three. The rain is easing a little. The co-op's extra crews are expected in from first light.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 04:00. That's the end of the live desk for tonight. If your lane flooded or your power went and you haven't told the co-op, do it in the morning; they've said they want every report. Thank you for listening, and dry your boots.

units.title: First night ferry in a week runs to time
units.author: courier
units.text: The first night crossing between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver for a week ran to time last night, with passengers describing the newly lit vessel as 'impossible to miss' as it crossed the Sound.

units.author: courier
units.text: The boat's own generator took over its deck lighting when shore power at Lisle failed during the night's cuts, and the temporary lighting tower on the Lisle slip switched to its own supply within seconds. Sound Lines said the night timetable would now continue as normal.

units.author: courier
units.text: The company has still not said what its crew welfare review found. In Gilliver, reports that a local teenager may have been responsible for one of the slipway sightings earlier in the month have circulated widely; the harbourmaster declined to comment beyond saying that any such matter would be 'dealt with quietly, with the family'.

units.title: Blackout falls keep emergency departments busy
units.author: weypost
units.text: Emergency departments in Weyhaven and Port Ammet have reported a rise in falls during this month's night-time power cuts, with sprained ankles and broken wrists among the most common injuries, many of them among older people on stairs.

units.author: weypost
units.text: 'It's always the same story,' said one senior nurse. 'Someone gets up when the lights go, carrying a candle or a phone, and misses the last step.' Hospital staff urged households to keep a torch by the bed and at the top and bottom of the stairs, and to carry one thing at a time.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Age charities said battery nightlights that switch on automatically when the mains fails were 'one of the cheapest and most effective things anyone can buy this winter', and asked neighbours to check on older residents living alone after any cut.

units.title: Salt, steel and cold snaps: why coastal networks trip
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: With night-time faults affecting a coastal distribution network in the Marrow Sound for a third week, engineers elsewhere in the industry say salt contamination on insulators is a well-understood problem, but one that usually follows a predictable pattern.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: 'Salt tracking shows up in damp, foggy, still conditions, typically at dawn,' said one consultant. 'You see the faults cluster in fog and then stop when it rains hard and washes the insulators. Faults on dry, clear, frosty nights are not what I'd expect from salt alone.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Other possible causes in cold weather include contraction of conductors, faulty protection settings and wildlife on poles. For forestry contractors working near overhead lines, the journal's usual advice applies: treat every line as live, and report any sag or unusual noise to the operator.

units.title: Cold spell breaks with rain and flood warnings
units.author: courier
units.text: The week-long calm, cold spell over the Sound ended today as rain spread in from the west from late morning, falling first on frozen ground and briefly turning roads and pavements to ice before temperatures rose.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Met Office has warned of heavy rain at times over the next three days, with southerly winds strengthening and a small-craft warning in force from this afternoon. Surface flooding is likely on low roads, including the reservoir lane at Brackwater, where culvert works are under way.

units.author: courier
units.text: Farmers welcomed the thaw but said the frost had damaged winter greens. The Brackwater estate asked walkers to keep away from the reservoir's outflow path and sluice, which flood quickly in heavy rain and where the clay banks become 'treacherous'.

units.title: As the Holm clearance nears its end, the owner says nothing
units.author: courier
units.text: By Nell Ashdown. With less than a week left on the contract to clear Kittering Holm of trees, its owner has still not said what the island is for. Ardent Vale Holdings has not responded to the Courier's questions for more than a week; its last public statement spoke of 'stewardship' and a 'long-term vision' without describing either.

units.author: courier
units.text: Planning records show only the vegetation clearance consent, which requires reseeding within two years. There is no application for building, power, water or a harbour. One planning consultant who has studied the file said it was 'exactly what you'd expect from someone who plans to sell the land on, cleared, at a profit'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Others are less sure. Online, theories range from a private retreat to a 'refuge' for the very wealthy. None is supported by any document the Courier has seen. Grieve Land Services, which holds the clearance contract, says it does not discuss its clients' intentions.

units.author: courier
units.text: Meanwhile the camp lights remain a nightly sight from Gilliver, where lamps have reappeared in many windows during the power cuts. 'Whatever the island's for, there are people out there working through the winter,' one resident said. 'That's the part I think about.'

units.title: Dellow Court lift back after maintenance
units.author: weypost
units.text: The lift at Dellow Court returned to service this afternoon after three hours of planned maintenance, during which residents on the upper floors relied on the stairs and on neighbours carrying shopping.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The shopkeeper on the ground floor kept heavy bags behind his counter and delivered them afterwards, and a group of residents has begun meeting in the lobby before dawn so that nobody has to use the stairs alone. 'It's become a sort of breakfast club,' said one.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it was 'considering' the residents' request for an independent survey of the building. The residents' association said the petition now had 47 signatures.

units.author: met
units.text: Forecast for the Marrow Sound, today and tonight. The cold spell ends. Cloudy, with rain spreading from the west by late morning, falling on frozen surfaces at first: risk of ice until temperatures rise. Southerly winds increasing 15 to 25 knots, gusting 35 on exposed coasts tonight. Rain heavy at times overnight. Maximum 7 °C, minimum 5 °C. Outlook: wet and windy for several days.

units.author: met
units.text: Small-craft warning, Marrow Sound, from 14:00 today until further notice. Southerly 5 to 6, occasionally 7 later. Sea state moderate, locally rough in the outer Sound and off Carrow Point. Visibility moderate in rain, poor at times.

units.author: met
units.text: Flood alert: Brackwater and the Tollinby valley. Heavy rain on frozen and saturated ground may cause surface flooding on low roads and paths from this evening, particularly near watercourses and culverts. Do not drive or walk through flood water. The reservoir outflow will run high.

units.author: met
units.text: Tides, Port Ammet reference. High water 05:33 (3.9 m) and 17:56 (4.1 m). Low water 11:44 and 23:58 (0.8 m). Strong southerly winds may raise levels by up to 0.3 m above prediction on the evening tide. Secure moorings before dark.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines service update. All sailings, including night sailings, are planned to operate today. Passengers should expect some movement on the crossing this evening as winds increase. Please hold handrails when boarding, keep to the lit deck areas, and allow extra time to reach the terminal in wet conditions.

units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines: the 22:40 sailing from Port Ammet departed at 22:47 due to late arrival of connecting passengers in heavy rain. Expected at Lisle 23:15 and Gilliver 23:50. The 00:15 return sailing may depart a few minutes late.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: overnight summary. Interruptions affected four circuits: Gilliver spur and Lisle pier (22:48 to 03:16), Port Ammet north (23:21 to 01:58) and Brackwater feeder (00:27 to 02:11). All customers are now on supply. Customers off for longer than the standard period may be entitled to a payment.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: additional resources. Four line crews from a neighbouring network arrive today to support patrols and repairs on the coastal and inland circuits. You may see unfamiliar vehicles on the Holm road and the coast road. Thank you for your patience and for giving crews room to work.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: night advisory. With rain and strong winds tonight, interruptions are possible across the network. Report any line that is down, sagging or sparking by calling our emergency number, and keep well clear. Please check the fault map before calling about loss of supply.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: momentary interruption, Gilliver spur, 23:51. Supply was restored automatically within about one minute. Some customers may have noticed lights dimming beforehand. No action is needed.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: unplanned interruption. Gilliver spur and Holm road from 01:30; Carrow Point and coast road from 01:41. Approximately 700 customers. A crew has been dispatched to the Gilliver switch. Estimated restoration 02:30.

units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: update. Gilliver spur restored 02:08. Carrow Point and coast road restored 02:57. A further momentary interruption on the Gilliver spur at 03:05 cleared automatically. All customers are now on supply.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: road closure. The Brackwater reservoir lane is closed at the culvert works due to flooding. Diversion via the Tollinby road. The lane will reopen when water levels fall and the culvert has been inspected. Please do not move the barriers.

units.author: council
units.text: Ammet District Council: waste collections. Delayed recycling collections in Port Ammet, including Rope Walk, were completed this morning. We thank our crews for opening the depot by hand in the early hours, and residents for their patience.

units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. Skerry buoy, east of Gilliver: the light remains unlit and servicing is postponed by the weather. Small craft are advised not to attempt the channel between Gilliver and Kittering Holm after dark until the light is restored and the small-craft warning is lifted.

units.title: Timesheet received KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Your timesheet for site KH-01, day 23, has been received and queued for processing. No exceptions were found. Reminder: period 3 closes at 23:59 tonight. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Period 3 closes tonight
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Period close notice. Site KH-01, period 3, closes at 23:59 Sound Time tonight. Timesheets and tree tallies entered after close will be carried into period 4. Settlement to the site account follows on the next banking day. Ref GLS-PC-0324. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Arrears: referral at period close
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Arrears notice. Site KH-01. Crew wages remain outstanding on the site account. If wages are outstanding at the close of period 3 (23:59 tonight), the account will be referred to Operations under the arrears procedure. Ref GLS-AR-0324. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Payment received, thank you
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Dear Policyholder, thank you. We have received your payment for policy LY-4471-0938 and your cover continues uninterrupted. Peace of mind, every month! Small print: please tell us if your circumstances change, including your place or type of work, as this may affect your cover.

units.title: The rain's coming! Are you ready?
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: The frost is over and the rain is on its way! Is your camp ready? Seal those seams, raise your stores off the ground, and keep a dry bag for the essentials. Our heavy-duty tarps are 20% off this week, and every order includes a free reflective guy-line kit so you'll never trip in the dark again!

units.title: Your stories: 'the lantern that saw us through'
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: This week's customer story comes from a reader on a remote site who wrote: 'Our Beacon ran all night for three weeks and never let us down. When the generator coughed, it was the only light we had.' Thank you for sharing! Send us your story and you could win a lantern of your own.

units.title: Rain and the boat
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper is running early this morning to get alongside before the wind gets up, so expect him well before midday. If he can't land the diesel because of the swell he'll bring it tomorrow instead. Please keep the landing clear and have two people ready on the lines. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Weekly note for head office
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a reminder that head office would like the short written note with this week's numbers: trees down, crew on site, anything that's slowing you. Three or four lines in the site log by tonight is plenty. With period 3 closing tonight, it would help to have the tally right up to date too. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Nearly there
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, quick one: the tally shows more than three-quarters of the Holm cleared. That's genuinely excellent work in that weather, and I've said so to head office in writing. Please don't let anyone push for the finish in the dark or the rain. The last quarter is where people get hurt. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The last week
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, I need to be honest about the tally. Under half the island is cleared with less than a week to go. Head office are asking me what went wrong and I'd rather tell them the truth from you than guess. Please put a few lines in the site log tonight: what's slowing you, and what would help. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Leaver's kit
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the stores team want to know whether the crew member who left took their company kit with them or left it on site. If it's still on the Holm, please bag it up and label it, and the skipper can bring it back on the next run. No hurry. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The dog
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the skipper mentioned that the dog's back with you safe and sound after its wander. I'm very glad. Head office needn't know the details. Please keep it in at night from now on, for its sake and for everyone's sleep. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Calls from families
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, after last night's power cuts we had several calls from crew families wanting to know the camp was all right. I told them the camp runs on its own generator and isn't affected by the mainland cuts, and that the supply boat runs on schedule. If anyone on the crew wants to pass a message home, put it in the site log and I'll ring it through. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Today's Courier
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, the Courier has a piece today about the owner not saying what the Holm is for. Nothing about the crew except that you're working hard, which is true. Head office have asked me again to remind everyone not to talk to the press, so consider yourself reminded. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Weather tonight
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, last one from me today. The Met Office has a small-craft warning out from this afternoon, so there'll be no boat movements tomorrow unless it eases. Please tie down anything loose in the yard, check the camper's guy lines, and keep everyone in after dark. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: first night!!
units.author: sam
units.text: the play happened!! first performance, in the afternoon so nobody walked home in the dark. ours was a cloud. the clouds wave their arms on the wrong beat and look extremely proud about it. she said her lines AND the extra one nobody wrote, which got the biggest laugh again. Mum didn't come, she's saving herself for the last one. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: it's pouring here. proper rain at last, the gutters are singing and the dog won't go out, he stands at the back door looking at me like I arranged it. the frost's all gone. I hope your roof's sound and your boots are dry. is it really fine out there? you'd tell me if it wasn't. love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: sorry, that sounded worried. I'm not worried. I'm a bit worried. the Courier's started saying 'the crew' like you're one thing, and Sound FM had a woman on talking about the lamps in Gilliver and she said 'for the island', and I sat in the car outside Mum's and didn't go in for ten minutes. silly. S x

units.title: from Mum, dictated
units.author: sam
units.text: Mum has dictated this and I'm typing it exactly: 'Tell them to wear a hat and to come home in one piece and that the hip is fine and the physio is a bully.' She's asleep now with the dog on her feet again. I've given up. S x

units.title: About my first email
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Hello, it's Morrow again. I'm sorry about my first email. I read it back and it must have been strange to get, from someone you don't know, who'd guessed your address. I didn't mean it to sound like anything. I won't write so often. I only wanted to apologise properly. Morrow

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong to add this. Your lights are on through the rain tonight. The low orange one went out early, I suppose the rain did that. The square one by the trees is lit. Someone on the Sound Board asked if you have a lamp in the window. I said I hoped so. Morrow

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Sorry, one more, then I'll stop. There was a thread on Lamp Hours tonight that I kept reading longer than I should have. It's closed now. I don't think it was about you. I just wanted someone to say that to you, in case you saw it. Goodnight. Morrow

units.title: From the archive: 'Gilliver Notes', December 1894
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: readers have asked whether the paper ever remarked on the timber camp's lights in the winter of 1894. It did, once, in the village column reproduced below from page 6. The correspondent was writing from the harbour; he did not visit the camp. As ever, he presents what he was told with more confidence than it deserves. G. Faulds.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The lights of the timber camp upon the Holm may now be seen from our harbour on any clear night, several lamps and a fire, burning till dawn, which is a novelty in a place that has been dark since the curing men left. Some of our older people have taken to answering them with a lamp of their own, which your correspondent finds very touching and wholly in keeping with the custom of the village.

units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: A boatman tells me the men have asked for oil by every boat, and more than was ordered. He supposes they read late. Another says they do not read at all but keep the lamps for company. Your correspondent, who has spent a winter night alone in a fishing hut, sides with the second, and wishes them a merry Christmas across the water.

units.title: Carrow Point log, December 1906 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 14th. 00:00 wind S 4, rain, vis 3 miles, barometer 29.81 falling fast. Lamp burning well. Fog signal not required. Remarks: none on the road, the weather being foul. Assistant says he slept well for the first time in a week and that he likes rain. I said so do I, and entered it here, which is not the purpose of the remarks column.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: 17th. 00:00 wind SW 5, showers, vis good between. Lamp burning well. 03:00 wind moderating. Remarks: one on the shore road at 03:30, at the bend, in a clear spell between showers. Gone in the next shower. Assistant on watch with me. He said 'there, you see,' and nothing else. I did not answer him.

units.title: Miss Arnell's notebook: loose page, species list for the Holm
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Holm, species recorded (one week). Birds: wren, goldcrest, robin, Turdus silvanus, redwing, raven (pr.), owl sp. (heard only), oystercatcher, curlew. Mammals: none. Not deer, not rabbit, not otter, not vole that I could trap. Insects: few, the season being late. Note to self: a list of absences is still a list. Do not let the Society print it with a question mark.

units.title: Amos Rendle's diary, 1936 (excerpts, cont.)
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 8. Wind come round SW in the night and rain with it, and the calm broke. Will was out of bed before me and had the boat baled by six. Said he slept like the dead. We did 7 boxes on the Holm side and he laughed all the way home at nothing. Mother says it was the calm that got him, and calms always pass.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 10. Blowing. No fishing. Mended pots. Will asked me tonight did I ever hear the Holm on a calm night, and I said everybody has, it carries. He said no, did I ever hear it answer. I said go to bed. Mother kept the lamp in as usual. I wrote this down because he asked me not to tell anyone.

units.title: Gilliver Oral History Project (1976): tape 26, side A
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Do you remember the timber camp on the Holm? / Mr H. Coad (b. 1886): I was eight. My uncle was foreman out there. / Interviewer: What do you remember? / Mr C.: The lights. You could see them from our window every night. Mother put our lamp in the window to answer them. Then one night they weren't there, and next day the men were home.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: Interviewer: Did your uncle say why they came home? / Mr C.: He said the pay was poor and the cold was worse. [pause] He said it so often I stopped believing it, if you follow. He never went to the Holm again, and he was a man who'd go anywhere for a shilling. / Interviewer: Did he keep a lamp? / Mr C.: Till the day he died. Two, after.

units.title: Talbot survey (1953): appendix A, party diary (concluded)
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Days 8 to 10. Tower foundations designed; landing surveyed at half tide; cost figures checked against the Board's schedule. Boat at 15:30, 15:15 and 15:00 respectively, at the party's request each day. Day 11. Pegs drawn, equipment embarked by 14:30. All present. The party returned to Gilliver in good order. Daylight working only throughout, as noted in section 5a.

units.title: LB-0588: Lisle ferry slip, night ambience (2011)
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LB-0588. Date: October 2011. Location: Lisle ferry slip, from the pier wall. Kit: handheld recorder, foam windshield. Duration: 51:30. Content: water on the slip, rigging from moored boats, the last ferry departing at 22:58. From 23:40, a slow, regular scraping near the foot of the slip, about every four seconds, for six minutes. Recordist's note: 'Weed and a loose chain, I think.' Curator's note: plausible.

units.title: Talk: Gilliver slipway, the 'man at the end of the slip'
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Talk note. Someone has added the 1976 tape about 'the fellow at the end of the slip' to the slipway article. The informant was eight at the time, misattributes him to a man already dead, and was describing a children's dare that existed precisely to frighten children. This is folklore about a game, not a record of anything. I have moved it to a footnote. Pell.

units.title: Gilliver slipway
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: The Gilliver slipway was built of granite setts in 1868, lengthened in 1931 and resurfaced in concrete in 1974. Byelaw 14, restricting access to the slip after dark, dates from 1931 and followed the drowning of a young man during what the harbour minutes call 'a foolish wager'. The slip is used by the Sound Lines ferry and by local boats; a temporary lighting tower was installed this month.
